meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And the zero itself, on what basis?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He wrote it over the weekend, and people paste in what they've drafted somewhere else. Turn the screen.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And before that zero went in, did anyone ask Owen where he drafted it?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time. And you skipped my question, Hale: was Owen asked before the zero?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Arguments change after an outline; that's what an outline is for. And since you won't answer, I'll take it nobody asked Owen.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Fine, you spoke to him the day before. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by a teacher he thinks has it in for him goes blank. What are you actually proposing, Hale?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at home with time to edit. I asked what you're proposing.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why bring it up. Put something on this table, Hale, or I'm walking down to the principal's office.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and in writing tonight. Private, not in front of his class, marked before December 1, and the promise that nothing goes on his file. On those terms he'll do it, to put this behind him.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
It works if it's marked before December 1, and the email is in my inbox tonight.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday. Put the time in tonight's email.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes, on Thursday, with the mark in before December 1.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
No, just the email tonight, the rewrite Thursday, and nothing on his file.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite on Thursday under procedure 4.4, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still need all of this confirmed in writing, including the time of the rewrite. I expect your email tonight, and the new mark entered before December 1.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight with the time and the mark entered before December 1; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her call.
What moved her: you answered her question about whether Owen was heard by showing your dated note of the November 2 conversation, because it was a checkable fact about process, which is what she trusts.
What cost ground: you let her question about whether anyone spoke to Owen go unanswered for two turns while you kept adding documents, which made her harder and slowed the turn.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's creation and nearly all its text between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, a late October night very close to what she feared; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she first asked whether Owen was spoken to before the zero, answer with the November 2 conversation straight away, before showing the quotation and the outline.
